title: Laine's family and home, rehearsals and schooling
summary: Laine says his father was a contractor and the family rented a nice home; he left school after he began playing for money.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Papa Lane, let me ask you this. When you were a little boy, when you first started playing, were you from a poor family? Was your family poor when you grew up?
Well, no, not exactly poor. If you want, no. What did your daddy do for a living? My daddy, he was a contractor, working with a contractor. He was a builder?

Yeah. I see. He had a nice home. Is that right? Y'all grew up in a nice home. Yeah. Now, these boys that played in your band at this political rally, were they poor or about like you were? Who's that? Those boys that played at that political rally. They weren't poor boys, were they? The boys that played at that political rally, you know, when you were 15 years old?
Those other boys in that band, now, were they poor or were they about like from the same kind of family you were?
Well, that I couldn't say. I couldn't say. But it looked like their family was pretty well. Pretty well healed.

You'd call them middle class, would you? You would call them middle class? Yeah, I'd call them middle class. I'm asking if they were working. Working people, though. Working people. Working people. I see. Did your daddy own his own home? Did your daddy own his home or did he rent? My daddy? Yes. No, we rent. You rent it. I see. We had a nice home. That's how they could all rehearse, you see. Ask them about those rehearsals.
Oh, that was at our place on Chard and Mandeville. It was a three-story place.
Where you rehearsal on Chard and Mandeville. That was our home when we lived there. There's where you rehearsal on Chard and Mandeville. That's right. In that basement. That was our home.
Yeah, that was our home. Yes. Well, you must have made good money. I did. I did. Whatever. I sent the two kids to school. Give them high education. All on music.
All on music. Did you go to school? Did you go to school? Did I go to school? Right. I went to school, but not so very much. I see.
Oh, I wouldn't have no idea.
